subject: mallard duck
title: Ducks Ate 8,000 Fish Eggs. A Few Came Out Alive and Hatched

scenes.text: Fish appear in ponds nobody stocked. Ducks may be carrying them, inside.
Scientists in Hungary fed about eight thousand carp eggs to eight mallard ducks.
Eighteen eggs came out intact in the droppings, up to a day later.
Twelve still had living embryos inside. Three of them hatched into baby fish.
That's only one egg in a few hundred. But a single carp can lay over a million eggs at once.
And a mallard can fly hundreds of kilometres between stops. That's how fish can fly.

description:
In a 2020 PNAS study, Hungarian researchers fed about 8,000 common and Prussian carp eggs to eight mallards; 18 eggs (0.2%) passed intact, 12 had living embryos, and three hatched.
With carp laying up to about 1.5 million eggs and mallards travelling long distances, ducks may explain fish turning up in isolated ponds.
Have you ever wondered how fish got into a pond?
first_comment: Only 0.2% made it through, but ducks eat a lot of eggs. Have you ever found fish in a pond nobody stocked?
